examples.text: And further, this examinate saith, that she sent both her spirits to Stonesby, to one Willison, a husbandman, and Robert Williman, a husbandman's son, and bade the kitten go to Willison and bewitch him to death, and the moldiwarp to the other and bewitch him to death, which they did, and within ten days they died.
Afterwards Jim said the witches bewitched him and put him in a trance,[…]

examples.text: I was bewitched by the sight of the girl dancing in the forest.

glosses: To astonish, amaze.

examples.text: Is it not a fact that the miners of this country are bewildered and bewitched and do not know what is to happen?

glosses: To attract and delight, to charm.

examples.text: New Jersey was reeling on Wednesday from the impact of Hurricane Sandy, which has caused catastrophic flooding here in Hoboken and in other New York City suburbs, destroyed entire neighborhoods across the state and wiped out iconic boardwalks in shore towns that had enchanted generations of vacationgoers.

examples.text: With the aid of his eponymous pipes, a satyr is capable of weaving a wide variety of melodic spells designed to enchant others and bring them in line with his capricious desires.

glosses: Someone, usually male, who uses (or has skill with) magic, mystic items, and magical and mystical practices.

examples.text: The wizard conjured up a large fireball.
The wily wizard must be caught.
He found himself watching a couple of wizards doing what he at first mistook for the beginning of a dance, and then for a session of tai chi. But suddenly he realized they were signing.
But that's not what will make her a powerful wizard – more powerful than me, more powerful than Leesha, even more powerful than you.

glosses: One who is especially skilled or unusually talented in a particular field.

examples.text: He was a financial wizard, capable of predicting the movements of the stock markets.

glosses: A computer program or script used to simplify complex operations, often for an inexperienced user.

examples.text: Use the "Add Network Connection" wizard to connect to a network in a series of simple steps.

glosses: A wise man; a sage.

examples.text: See how from far upon the eastern road / The star-led wizards [Magi] haste with odours sweet!

glosses: To practice wizardry.

To place under the influence of a magical spell; to enchant or bewitch with a spell.
To captivate, or hold the attention of, as if by a magic spell; to entrance.
Troubler physiquement ou moralement par de prétendus sortilèges.

examples.text: Elle avoua que depuis long-temps, et de concert avec le démon, elle avait pratiqué la magie et les maléfices, qu’elle avait positivement ensorcelé la pauvre madame Lutkens.

glosses: Troubler par une violente passion, un amour qui va jusqu’à la folie, jusqu’à la fureur.

examples.text: Nous avons appris tout à la fois le funeste destin de Front-de-Bœuf, et ta fuite avec cette belle sorcière juive dont les yeux noirs t’ont ensorcelé.

glosses: Captiver.

examples.text: Est-ce l’atmosphère de cete ville qui m’ensorcelle?
Vous nous ensorcelez, vous enchantez nos sens.

glosses: Produire un effet extraordinaire sur quelqu’un ou sur quelque chose par un charme magique.

examples.text: Orphée, dit-on, charmait hommes, bêtes et arbres par les accents de sa lyre.

glosses: Fasciner.

examples.text: Le serpent charme les oiseaux.

glosses: Plaire extrêmement ; ravir en admiration ; séduire.

examples.text: Non, non, la constance n'est bonne que pour des ridicules ; toutes les belles ont droit de nous charmer, et l'avantage d'être rencontrée la première ne doit pas dérober aux autres les justes prétentions qu'elles ont toutes sur nos cœurs.

examples.text: Vous me charmez en m’apprenant cela. Je suis charmé de vous voir. Il sera charmé de cette nouvelle.
